title: The Three Counsels of the Little Nightingale

keywords: history of what befel the fowl-let with the fowler
full_text:
A hunter in Syria caught a tiny, radiant nightingale in his snare. As he drew his knife to slaughter the little bird for a morsel of meat, the nightingale spoke in musical, human words:

'O hunter! My flesh will not fill thy stomach, nor will my tiny bones satisfy thy hunger. But if thou wilt set me free, I will teach thee three priceless counsels that will bring thee wisdom and prosperity for the rest of thy days.'

The fowler, astonished, agreed: 'Tell me thy counsels, and I will release thee.'
The nightingale said:
'The first counsel I give thee while still in thy hand: Never weep over that which is lost and gone, for tears cannot reverse the past.'

The fowler loosened his grip, and the bird flew to a low branch:
'The second counsel I give thee from this branch: Never believe that which is contrary to reason, no matter who tells it to thee.'

The bird then soared to the highest branch of a tall cedar, looked down, and called out:
'O foolish hunter! If thou hadst slain me, thou wouldst have found inside my gizzard an enormous pearl weighing ten ounces, which would have made thee the richest prince in Damascus!'

The fowler bit his hands in furious regret, tore his garments, and wept:
'Woe is me! What a treasure I have lost! Come back to me, sweet bird, and I will feed thee sugar in a golden cage!'

The nightingale laughed musically:
'O blind man! How quickly hast thou forgotten the first two counsels!
First: I told thee never to weep over what is lost, yet thou art tearing thy coat in tears over my escape!
Second: I told thee never to believe what is impossible, yet thou didst believe that my tiny body, which weighs barely two ounces, could contain a pearl weighing ten ounces!
And now hear the third counsel, which is the seal of wisdom:
Never waste precious words of wisdom upon a fool whose heart is blinded by greed, for to him, gold dust and mountain dirt are the same.'

With that, the little nightingale spread its wings and flew into the azure sky, leaving the fowler to ponder the true wealth of understanding.
moral: Do not weep over past losses, do not believe the impossible, and do not waste pearls of wisdom on the foolish.
